subject: Luminexa discovery follow-up — trial definition & model shortlist
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Hammond <sara@luminexa.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro call — quick recap and suggested trial definition

Sara — thanks again for the chat today. Quick recap and a concrete trial definition we can align on so the engineering team can try things next week. Please review and flag anything missing.

1) Goals (what success looks like for Luminexa)
- Intent accuracy: >=90% for EN, >=85% for FR/ES on the initial 1k utterance seed set.
- Latency: model p95 generation latency <= 400ms at expected throughput (see throughput below).
- Cost: target inferred cost per 1k sessions to fit within the budget line in the attached MVP scope.
- Safety/PII: no persistent logging of raw customer text; redact PII where detected.

2) Scope & languages
- Initial scope: search-assist and checkout-help flows for EN, FR, ES.
- Data: we’ll use the synthetic + production-like seed set (you mentioned a 1k corpus) and the two anonymized CS transcripts you shared.

3) Proposed trial model shortlist (primary + fallback) — initial recommendation from our inference bench:
- Primary (generation + multilingual): Open-Redwood-16k-v1 (8-bit quantized variant for latency) — balanced cost/quality for short dialogues.
- Fallback (fast, cheap): mBART-50-lite (quantized) for FR/ES heavy traffic or when we need strict latency.
- Safety/strict parsing tasks: small deterministic reranker (linear model) for transactional extraction.

4) Evaluation plan & acceptance criteria
- Automated eval: intent/slot F1, hallucination rate (manual spot checks), latency distribution (p50/p95), token cost. Thresholds as above.
- Human eval: 30-minute blind review sessions across EN/FR/ES with CS SMEs; acceptance requires >=8/10 productiveness score.

5) Timeline & owners (proposed)
- Nov 10: Share baseline eval rubric + Drive folder (Jordan) — attached rubric csv.
- Nov 11–13: Redwood runs baseline inference across shortlist on sample dataset; returns metrics (Marissa).
- Nov 16: Joint review call to confirm model and fallback choices; agree canary gating (Sara + Luminexa eng).
- Nov 23: Start 2-week canary (Aditya to coordinate deployment config).

6) Open questions for you
- Confirm throughput expectation: you mentioned 200–300 QPS peak — can you confirm expected average QPS and concurrency on the pilot flows?
- Any additional compliance constraints beyond the PDF you attached (PII handling, retention windows)?

Attachments: Luminexa_MVP_scope.xlsx, trial-eval-rubric.csv (stubbed).

Thanks — if that plan looks reasonable I’ll kick off the baseline run tomorrow and share results by EOD Friday.

—
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0142

From: Sara Hammond <sara@luminexa.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Luminexa Engineering <eng@luminexa.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro call — quick recap and suggested trial definition

Jordan — thanks for the clear write-up, this is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Throughput: target peak is ~250 QPS for the search-assist flow, but average is closer to 40 QPS; concurrency spikes are often short (<2 minutes).
- Languages: EN covers 80% of traffic; FR/ES about 15% combined. We will prioritize EN quality but need FR/ES to be reliable for checkout flows.
- Compliance: retention window must be <=30 days for customer transcripts; we need an option to disable KV cache for specific routes.
- Budget: per-conversation token cap is tight — please include costed estimates for the primary model vs a smaller quantized fallback.

I attached Luminexa_privacy_reqs.pdf to this reply (we share it with vendors). Also noted: we prefer early canary traffic to be routed from a non-prod region (us-west) to limit blast radius.

If you can update the rubric with latency buckets and a cost column, that would be great. Otherwise we’re aligned to the proposed dates.

—
Sara Hammond
Head of Product, Luminexa
sara@luminexa.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Hammond <sara@luminexa.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro call — quick recap and suggested trial definition

Thanks Sara — good notes. Quick update with concrete POC actions and a refined model selection to address throughput, latency, and budget constraints.

[On Tue, 10 Nov 2026 at 09:18 AM Sara Hammond <sara@luminexa.com> wrote:]
> Jordan — thanks for the clear write-up, this is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 
> - Throughput: target peak is ~250 QPS for the search-assist flow, but average is closer to 40 QPS...

Redwood proposed actions (detailed):
A) Baseline runs (Nov 11–13) — what we will measure per model variant:
- Intent accuracy (micro-average) on the seed 1k set.
- p50/p95 token-generation latency measured at 40 QPS and simulated 250 QPS (burst).
- Token cost per 1k requests with the same prompt set.
- Safety flags: heuristic PII detection hit rate.

B) Model shortlist (refined)
- Primary candidate — Open-Redwood-16k-v1 (int8 quant)
  - Why: good EN quality, supports longer context for follow-ups; measured p95 ~350ms at 40 QPS on our dedicated node.
- Secondary candidate — Llama-2-13B-instruct-q4 (fast quantized variant)
  - Why: lower token cost and p95 ~220–300ms under load; acceptable EN quality but slightly worse on nuanced FR/ES phrasing.
- Fallback — mBART-50-finetune-lite (small multilingual model)
  - Why: deterministic multilingual coverage for FR/ES where Llama-variants drop below threshold.

C) Canary gating & routing
- Route 5% traffic to the primary candidate for first 48 hours; if p95 < 450ms and intent accuracy loss <5% vs baseline, expand to 25% for next 7 days.
- If FR/ES quality dips, route FR/ES to fallback model until we retrain/adjust prompts.
- Disable KV caching for checkout-help route until we confirm PII redaction. (We’ll provide a toggle you can flip.)

D) Evaluation rubric (I updated the attached CSV) — key columns added: p50, p95 latency (ms), token_cost_per_1k, intent_accuracy, manual_hallucination_rate, pass/fail. Acceptance = pass across at least 2/3 metrics and no critical safety failures.

E) Timeline (refined owners)
- Nov 11 (today): Jordan to upload updated rubric + baseline config to Drive (done).
- Nov 11–13: Marissa to run bench and return results (artifacts: latency histograms, cost calc, model outputs).
- Nov 16: Review call — decide on canary gating and quantization config (Jordan + Sara + Luminexa eng + Marissa).
- Nov 23–Dec 7: Canary window (Aditya coordinates infra + canary routing).

F) Deliverables we’ll ship to you by Nov 13
- Per-model metrics CSV + sample outputs for 200 seed prompts.
- Recommended runtime config (batching, KV cache settings, quantization profile).
- Estimated token cost spreadsheet (low/med/high traffic scenarios).

G) Quick ask: please confirm the two anonymized transcript files we should use, and confirm we can run the baseline in us-west for canary.

Attachments referenced: trial-eval-rubric.csv (updated), Luminexa_MVP_scope.xlsx.

If that aligns I’ll schedule the Nov 16 review and share the bench results on Monday EOD.

—
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Jordan — this is great, thanks. Confirming:
- We approve the baseline runs (use our two anonymized transcripts: transcript_A_redacted.txt, transcript_B_redacted.txt).

Please proceed with the benchmark and we’ll be on the Nov 16 call to lock the canary config. One additional ask: include a column for data retention windows in the cost spreadsheet so we can confirm the 30-day retention constraint.

Sara Hammond
